SK1.claim: Sikkim is home to Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain and India's highest, and to the UNESCO-listed Khangchendzonga National Park.

evidence.quote: It is home to the Kanchenjunga National Park , a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and boasts the Kanchenjunga Peak, India's loftiest summit.
offers stunning views of the Kanchenjunga range, the world’s third-highest mountain.

SK2.claim: Sikkim has banned plastic water bottles, one of India's most environmentally conscious states.

evidence.quote: Sikkim has demonstrated its commitment to environmental conservation by prohibiting the use of plastic water bottles

SK3.claim: Sikkimese food blends Tibetan, Nepali and Lepcha cooking; it is also home to the fiery Dalle Khorsani chilli.

evidence.quote: Sikkimese food is a harmonious fusion of Tibetan, Nepali, and Lepcha influences
The state is renowned for producing the scorching hot Dalle Khorsani chili

SK4.claim: The Indian Army controls large border areas of Sikkim; many are restricted and need permits.

evidence.quote: The Indian Army has control of a large territory, as the state is a sensitive border area. Many areas are restricted, and permits are needed to visit them.

SK5.claim: Bagdogra airport near Siliguri is the gateway to Gangtok; Sikkim's Pakyong airport has no operating flights at present.

evidence.quote: It is the gateway to the hill stations of Darjeeling , Gangtok , Kurseong , Kalimpong , Mirik
However, the resumption proved short lived and at present there are no operational flights from Pakyong.

GT1.claim: Gangtok, Sikkim's capital, sits at 1,650 m with a mild climate — about 22°C at most in summer and 5°C at night in winter.

evidence.quote: is the capital and the most populous city of the Indian state of Sikkim
at an elevation of 1,650 m (5,410 ft)
Temperatures range from an average maximum of 22 °C (72 °F ) in summertime to an average minimum of 5 °C (41 °F) in winter.

GT2.claim: Bagdogra airport is about 124 km — some five hours' drive — from Gangtok.

evidence.quote: Bagdogra , located 124 km (77 mi) (and a five-hour drive) away in the neighboring state of West Bengal

GT3.claim: MG Marg is the main promenade; Do-drul Chorten, Ganesh Tok and the Tashi Viewpoint, with views of Khangchendzonga, are classic stops.

evidence.quote: Take a stroll through MG Marg, the city's main promenade
Do-drul Chorten is marked by a golden dome
On clear days, visitors can enjoy stunning views of Mt. Khangchendzonga, Mt. Siniolchu , and the vibrant villages of North Sikkim from the Tashi Viewpoint.

GTN1.claim: The Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, about 5 km south in Deorali, holds the largest collection of Tibetan works outside Tibet.

evidence.quote: boasts the largest collection of Tibetan works outside Tibet. Located in Deorali, south of Gangtok, about 5 km away, it includes a museum, a research center, and a library.

GTR1.claim: Rumtek, the Dharma Chakra Centre near Gangtok, is the seat in exile of the Karmapa, inaugurated in 1966.

evidence.quote: also called the Dharma Chakra Centre , is a gompa located in the Indian state of Sikkim near the capital Gangtok . It is the seat in exile of the Gyalwang Karmapa, inaugurated in 1966 by the 16th Karmapa.

GTR2.claim: A golden stupa holds the relics of the 16th Karmapa.

evidence.quote: A golden stupa contains the relics of the 16th Karmapa.

GTT1.claim: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake lies at 12,313 ft and is sacred to the Sikkimese; open 7:30 am–4:30 pm, with yak rides.

evidence.quote: Perched at an altitude of 12,313 feet above sea level, Tsomgo Lake, also known as Changu Lake
it's a sacred site for the Sikkimese
There is a provision to take rides on yaks and mules here

GTT2.claim: Beyond the lake are the Kyongnosla Alpine Sanctuary, Nathu La and Hangu Lake.

evidence.quote: Beyond the lake, one can visit the Kyongnosla Alpine sanctuary, Nathu La Pass as well as Hangu Lake.

GTN2.claim: Nathu La, 56 km from Gangtok on the India–China border, is one of the highest motorable roads in the world.

evidence.quote: Nathu la Pass is one of the highest motorable roads in the world that lies at a distance of 56 km from Gangtok.

GTN3.claim: Only Indian citizens may visit, Thursday to Sunday, with permits obtained a day ahead in Gangtok.

evidence.quote: On the Indian side, only citizens of India can visit the pass on Thursdays to Sundays, after obtaining permits one day in advance in Gangtok.

PL1.claim: Pelling, in West Sikkim at 2,150 m, has close views of the Kanchenjunga range.

evidence.quote: Standing at an elevation of 2,150 meters (7,050 feet), Pelling is a haven for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

PL2.claim: Nearby are the Rabdentse ruins, the former royal capital, the Tashiding Monastery and Yuksom, a trekking base.

evidence.quote: discover Rabdentse, the erstwhile royal capital hidden amidst ruins.
The Tashiding Monastery , nestled in the verdant hills of West Sikkim, is a revered pilgrimage site associated with Guru Padmasambhava
The nearby Yuksom Valley is a popular trekking destination

PLP1.claim: Pemayangtse, 'Perfect Sublime Lotus', became a monastery in 1705 and is Sikkim's second-oldest after Dubdi; open 8 am–4 pm.

evidence.quote: Pemayangtse translates to "Perfect Sublime Lotus"
Today, it is considered the second-oldest monastery in Sikkim, after Dubdi Monastery.

PLP2.claim: Over a hundred monks live here; masked dances are held at the Guru Drakmar Chamm festival.

evidence.quote: With over one hundred monks diligently upholding its sacred practices
traditional dances are performed during the annual Guru Drakmar Chamm festival.

PLK1.claim: Khecheopalri Lake is revered as a wish-fulfilling lake by Buddhists and Hindus.

evidence.quote: The Khecheopalri Lake , also known as the "Wishing Lake," is revered by Buddhists and Hindus alike

PLN1.claim: Khangchendzonga National Park, a UNESCO site of 1,784 sq km, has 18 glaciers, including the 26 km Zemu Glacier, and 17 alpine lakes.

evidence.quote: This stunning park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site spread over 1784 square kilometres.
you'll be captivated by the sight of 18 glaciers, including the renowned Zemu Glacier (about 26 km long), and 17 shimmering alpine lakes

PLN2.claim: Red pandas, snow leopards and musk deer live here; the land is sacred to Buddhists and Lepchas.

evidence.quote: including the elusive red pandas, majestic snow leopards, great Tibetan sheep, bharals, and graceful musk deer
the park is also considered sacred by both Buddhists (Beyul) and Lepchas as Mayel Lyang

NS1.claim: Mangan is the gateway to North Sikkim and Gurudongmar Lake; Dzongu is a reserved area of the Lepcha community.

evidence.quote: Mangan serves as the gateway to the revered Gurudongmar Lake
Dzongu: A reserved area for the Lepcha community

NSL1.claim: Lachung, at about 9,600 ft, sits where the Lachen and Lachung rivers meet; visitors come October to May on the way to Yumthang.

evidence.quote: Lachung is at an elevation of about 9,600 feet (2,900 m) and at the confluence of the Lachen and Lachung Rivers
Tourists come from all over the world between October and May, mostly on their way to the Yumthang Valley

NSY1.claim: Yumthang, Sikkim's 'Valley of Flowers' at about 3,564 m, has hot springs and the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary; flowers bloom late February to mid June.

evidence.quote: The Yumthang Valley or Sikkim Valley of Flowers sanctuary , is a nature sanctuary with river, hot springs, yaks and grazing pasture
It is at an elevation of 3,564 metres (11,693 ft) above msl
The flowering season is from late February and to mid June

NSY2.claim: Yumthang is closed December to March due to heavy snow.

evidence.quote: Yumthang is closed between December and March due to heavy snowfall.

NSG1.claim: Gurudongmar Lake, at 5,430 m, is one of the highest lakes in the world, 190 km from Gangtok and about 5 km from the Chinese border.

evidence.quote: Gurudongmar Lake is one of the highest lakes in the world and in India , at an elevation of 5,430 m (17,800 ft) according to the Government of Sikkim
190 km (120 mi) from Gangtok , and about 5 km (3.1 mi) south of the Chinese border.

NSG2.claim: It is reached on NH310C from Chungthang via Lachen and Thangu.

evidence.quote: The lake can be reached by the 100-kilometre-long (62 mi) National Highway 310C (NH310C) from Chungthang via Lachen and Thangu Valley .

MG1.claim: Meghalaya's Khasi and Jaintia peoples belong to one of the world's largest surviving matrilineal cultures; its living root bridges are on UNESCO's tentative list.

evidence.quote: Meghalaya's indigenous people belong to one of the world's largest matrilineal cultures still existing today.
Recently added to UNESCO's tentative world heritage site list

MG2.claim: Guwahati's airport, the main airport of Northeast India, is the usual gateway; Shillong also has an airport at Umroi.

evidence.quote: It is the primary airport of Northeast India .
the nearest airport is Shillong Airport or Umroi Airport

SH1.claim: Shillong, Meghalaya's capital, was the capital of undivided Assam until Meghalaya was formed in 1972.

evidence.quote: Shillong was the capital of composite Assam during the British regime and for 25 years in independent India until a separate State of Meghalaya was formed in 1972.

SH2.claim: The 16-km David Scott Trail is a classic hike through the East Khasi Hills.

evidence.quote: This ancient 16-kilometer path, named after a British administrator

SHP1.claim: Shillong Peak, at 1,965 m, is sacred to the Khasi and Jaintia; open 9 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: Perched at an impressive altitude of 6,449 feet (1,965 meters) above sea level
revered as a sacred place where tribal rituals and ceremonies are performed

SHW1.claim: Ward's Lake, a horseshoe-shaped lake of 1894, has a botanical garden around it.

evidence.quote: brought to life by the skilled hands of Colonel Hopkins in 1894. What sets this 100-year-old lake apart is its unique horseshoe shape and the lush botanical garden that surrounds it

SHE1.claim: Elephant Falls drops in three tiers; the British named it for an elephant-shaped rock lost in an earthquake. Open 6 am–6 pm.

evidence.quote: the present name was given by the British after an elephant-shaped rock here, which was lost to an earthquake over a century ago.

SHD1.claim: The Don Bosco Museum, set up in 2003, shows the cultures of Northeast India's tribes; open Tuesday to Saturday, 9:30 am–5:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Don Bosco Museum was set up in 2003 by the Salesians of Don Bosco, to preserve and promote the rich and diverse culture of North-eastern tribes.

SHU1.claim: Umiam Lake (Bara Pani) is a reservoir 15 km north of Shillong, made by damming the Umiam River in the early 1960s.

evidence.quote: is a reservoir in the hills 15 km (9.3 mi) north of Shillong in the state of Meghalaya , India . It was created by damming the Umïam River in the early 1960s.

SHL1.claim: Laitlum, 'end of hills', is a hilltop with sweeping views over deep gorges in the East Khasi Hills.

evidence.quote: Laitlum, meaning "end of hills," is a mesmerising hilltop that offers panoramic views of the surrounding valleys and gorges.

SHM1.claim: Mawphlang Sacred Grove, about 78 hectares, has been protected by the Khasi community for centuries.

evidence.quote: Spread over an area of approximately 78 hectares, this ancient forest is revered by the local Khasi community and has been preserved for centuries as a sacred site.

SHK1.claim: In Kongthong, 60 km from Shillong, each newborn is given a melody that becomes their lifelong name.

evidence.quote: 60 kilometres from Shillong, lies a fascinating valley region, in the East Khasi Hills, named Khat-ar-shnong, referred to as the Whistling village of Meghalaya.
the gift of a melody bestowed upon each newborn, a tune that becomes their lifelong unique ID.

SHN1.claim: Mawlynnong, 90 km from Shillong near the Bangladesh border, was named Asia's cleanest village by Discover India magazine.

evidence.quote: It is notable for its cleanliness and also was chosen by Discover India magazine as Asia's cleanest village.
Mawlynnong is located 90 km from Shillong

CH1.claim: Cherrapunji (Sohra), about 50 km from Shillong, still holds the records for the most rain in a month and a year.

evidence.quote: The town is located around 50 kilometers from Shillong
Sohra still holds the all-time record for the most rainfall in a calendar month and in a year

CH2.claim: November to February is the drier season, best for falls, caves and root bridges.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Cherrapunjee is undoubtedly during winter, from November to February.

CHN1.claim: Nohkalikai Falls, about 340 m, is India's tallest plunge waterfall; viewpoint open 9 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: Towering at an astonishing 340 meters, it is the tallest plunge waterfall in India.

CHM1.claim: Mawsmai is a limestone cave stretching about 820 ft; open 9 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: Cherrapunji also boasts stunning limestone caves and its Mawsmai Cave, stretches 820 feet into the earth.

CHB1.claim: The trek to Nongriat's double-decker root bridge starts at Tyrna and descends about 3,500 steps.

evidence.quote: This route begins from Tyrna village, involving a descent of about 3500 steps.

CHB2.claim: The bridges are grown from rubber fig roots by the Khasi and Jaintia peoples.

evidence.quote: The structures are handmade from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees ( Ficus elastica

AS1.claim: Assam is India's largest tea producer, with nearly half the country's output.

evidence.quote: Assam is the largest tea producer in India and is responsible for nearly half of the country's total tea production.

AS2.claim: Guwahati's Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi airport, at Borjhar about 28 km from the city, is the main airport of the Northeast.

evidence.quote: It is the primary airport of Northeast India . It is located at Borjhar , 26 km (16 mi) from Dispur and 28 km (18 mi) from Guwah

GH1.claim: Guwahati, ancient Pragjyotishpura, is Assam's largest city and home of the Kamakhya Temple.

evidence.quote: Explore Guwahati, the ancient city which was once known as Pragjyotishpura.

GHK1.claim: The Kamakhya Temple, on Nilachal hill 8 km from the city, is one of India's most important pilgrimage sites and a great centre of Tantric worship.

evidence.quote: Perched on Nilachal hill, 8 km (5 miles) northwest of the city, the Kamakhya Temple is one of India’s most important pilgrimage destinations.
is one of the oldest and most revered centres of Tantric practices

GHK2.claim: It hosts the annual Ambubachi Mela.

evidence.quote: the site of the Ambubachi Mela , an annual festival that celebrates the menstruation of the goddess.

GHU1.claim: The 16th-century Umananda Temple stands on Peacock Island in the Brahmaputra.

evidence.quote: Enchantingly located on the lush green Peacock Island in the middle of the Brahmaputra, this 16th-century Umananda Temple

GHS1.claim: Sualkuchi, 32 km from Guwahati, is the great weaving centre for golden muga and paat silk.

evidence.quote: Sualkuchi, 32 km (20 miles) west of Guwahati, is a major weaving centre for Assam’s famous golden-hued muga and paat silk.

KZ1.claim: Kaziranga, a UNESCO site on the Brahmaputra, holds two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinos and a high density of tigers.

evidence.quote: Kaziranga National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceros find sanctuary!
Kaziranga was declared a Tiger Reserve in 2007 .

KZ2.claim: The park has the world's largest populations of Indian rhinos (2,401), wild water buffalo and eastern swamp deer.

evidence.quote: The park has the distinction of being home to the world's largest population of the Indian rhinoceros (2,401)

KZ3.claim: Kaziranga is about two hours from Tezpur; park hours are 7 am to 5:45 pm.

evidence.quote: just a scenic two-hour drive from Tezpur

KZ4.claim: In July and August, about three-quarters of the western park floods.

evidence.quote: During the peak months of July and August, three-fourths of the western region of the park is submerged

MJ1.claim: Majuli, in the Brahmaputra, is recognised by Guinness as the world's largest inland river island, and is the hub of Assamese neo-Vaishnavite culture.

evidence.quote: Majuli is recognized by Guinness World Records as the world's largest inland river island
serves as a hub of Assamese neo- Vaishnavite culture.

MJ2.claim: Majuli is reached by ferry or boat from Jorhat, about 250 km from Guwahati.

evidence.quote: It is accessible by ferry or boat from Jorhat , which is located approximately 250 kilometers northeast of Guwahati .

MJ3.claim: Sankardev founded satras (monasteries) here in the 16th century; the Misings are the island's largest tribal community.

evidence.quote: propagated Vaishnavism and established monasteries (known as satras ) on the island.
you'll meet the Misings, the largest tribal community

MJA1.claim: The Auniati Satra, founded in 1653 under the Ahom king Jayadhwaj Singha, is known for Sattriya dance; open 6 am–6 pm.

evidence.quote: Founded in 1653 AD under the patronage of the Ahom king Jayadhwaj Singha
The mesmerizing Sattriya Nritya dance-drama will transport you back to the 15th and 16th centuries

SV1.claim: Sivasagar is an enclave of Ahom palaces and monuments: the Rang Ghar, the seven-storey Kareng Ghar and the great Sivasagar tank.

evidence.quote: One of the most iconic heritage destinations of Assam is Sivasagar, an enclave of Ahom palaces and monuments.
the Kareng Ghar, a royal palace with seven floors and secret underground passages

SVR1.claim: The two-storey Rang Ghar, built in 1746, is called Asia's oldest amphitheatre; kings watched games and bullfights from it. Open 9 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: It was built in 1746 as a place of entertainment for the royal families
It is the oldest amphitheatre in Asia.

SVR2.claim: Its roof is shaped like a royal Ahom boat, and its mortar used rice paste, eggs and fish.

evidence.quote: The structure's unique roof mimics the shape of a royal Ahom boat
Ahom builders created a special mortar using rice paste, eggs, and Borali fish.

SVC1.claim: Charaideo, about 30 km from Sivasagar, has the moidams — the 'Pyramids of Assam' — burial mounds of Ahom royalty. Open 9:30 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: take a short trip to Charaideo Moidam, which is about 30 kilometres from the city. People call these burial mounds the "Pyramids of Assam"

MN1.claim: Manas, over 950 sq km on the Bhutan border, is a UNESCO site, tiger reserve and biosphere reserve with over 450 bird species. Open 7 am–4 pm.

evidence.quote: Spanning over 950 sq km, this protected area is a UNESCO Natural World Heritage site and a Biosphere Reserve
with over 450 species of birds, including the rare Bengal florican, great hornbill, and black-necked stork.

MN2.claim: It shelters pygmy hogs, hispid hares and golden langurs.

evidence.quote: It also harbours endemic species like pygmy hog, hispid hare and golden langur

HG1.claim: Hoollongapar, in Jorhat district, protects western hoolock gibbons — India's only ape — and at least 219 bird species.

evidence.quote: Home to the western hoolock gibbons, the only species of gibbons in India
With at least 219 species flitting above you

AR1.claim: Arunachal Pradesh is the largest of the Northeast's seven sister states, with over 500 orchid species.

evidence.quote: Arunachal Pradesh is the largest among the seven sister states in North east India.
Within its lush jungles lies over 500 rare orchid species.

AR2.claim: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit to enter Arunachal Pradesh; a tourist ILP is valid for 15 days, and can be applied for online as an e-ILP.

evidence.quote: It is required for entering Arunachal Pradesh through any of the check points across the interstate border with Assam or Nagaland . An ILP for temporary visitors is valid for 15 days and can be extended
has developed a online web based application to issue Tourist eILP

TW1.claim: Tawang sits at about 3,000 m, 448 km by road from Itanagar.

evidence.quote: It is situated 448 km by road north-west of state capital Itanagar at an elevation of approximately 3,000 metres (10,000 ft) .

TW2.claim: Besides the monastery, see the Tawang War Memorial and Nuranang (Jang) Falls.

evidence.quote: Don't miss the chance to visit the Nuranang Waterfall , also known as the Jang Falls
head to the Tawang War Memorial

TWM1.claim: Founded in 1680–81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso at the wish of the 5th Dalai Lama, Tawang is India's largest Buddhist monastery.

evidence.quote: It is the largest Buddhist monastery in the country.
It was founded by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso in 1680–1681 in accordance with the wishes of the 5th Dalai Lama

TWM2.claim: It houses a 28-foot statue of the Buddha; the name Tawang means 'chosen by horse'.

evidence.quote: The Tawang Monastery houses a 28-foot-tall statue of Lord Buddha
So, the word Tawang means "chosen by horse".

TWW1.claim: The Tawang War Memorial, a stupa, honours 2,420 servicemen who died in the 1962 war; open 7:45 am–6 pm.

evidence.quote: The memorial was built in memory of the 2,420 members of the armed forces who
This stupa stands as a poignant testament to the brave Indian soldiers who laid down their lives during the 1962 Indo-China War.

TWJ1.claim: Jaswant Garh, 25 km from Tawang at 10,000 ft, honours rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, who held his post for 72 hours in 1962.

evidence.quote: located just 25 kilometres from Tawang at an altitude of 10,000 feet
For 72 gruelling hours, he single-handedly inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy

TWS1.claim: Sela Pass, at 4,170 m, links Tawang with Dirang and the rest of India; it is 78 km from Tawang.

evidence.quote: It has an elevation of 4170 m (13,700 ft) and connects the Indian Buddhist town of Tawang to Dirang
is situated at a distance of 78 km from Tawang town and 340 km from Guwahati .

TWS2.claim: The BRO keeps the pass open, but snow can close it temporarily; the Sela Tunnel was built as an all-weather route.

evidence.quote: While the Border Roads Organization (BRO) of India works to keep the pass open throughout the year, it may shut down temp
Government of India announced the funding for construction of all weather road transport tunnel

DR1.claim: Dirang's Thembang is a 9th-century fortified village on UNESCO's candidate list.

evidence.quote: One of its must-visit attractions is Thembang Zong, a 9th-century fortified village

BM1.claim: Bomdila Monastery (GRL), set up in 1965, has three sections; Bomdila is 160 km from Tezpur and 340 km from Guwahati.

evidence.quote: Established in 1965 and inspired by South Tibet’s Tsona Gontse Monastery
It is approximately 160 km from Tezpur and 340 km from Guwahati.

BM2.claim: Tezpur airport, 160 km away, is nearest; Rangapara North station is about 95 km.

evidence.quote: Tezpur Airport (TEZ) is the nearest airport, situated about 160 km from Bomdila.
Rangapara North Railway Station (RGPP) is the nearest major railhead, located approximately 95 km from Bomdila.

ZR1.claim: Ziro, at about 1,500 m and 165 km from Itanagar, is home to the Apatani and their paddy-cum-fish farming; it was shortlisted for UNESCO in 2012.

evidence.quote: Located at an elevation of about 1,500 metres, nearly 165 km from Itanagar
Shortlisted in 2012 for UNESCO World Heritage Site status, the valley is renowned for its unique paddy-cum-pisciculture system practised by the indigenous Apatani tribe

overview.text:
Sikkim sits in the Eastern Himalayas beneath Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain and India's highest, and is home to the UNESCO-listed Khangchendzonga National Park. It is a green state too — plastic water bottles are banned.

Gangtok, the capital, is the base for Rumtek Monastery, Tsomgo Lake and Nathu La. West Sikkim's Pelling has close views of the Kanchenjunga range and the Pemayangtse Monastery; North Sikkim rises to the Yumthang Valley and Gurudongmar Lake, one of the highest lakes in the world.

overview.text:
Meghalaya's Khasi and Jaintia peoples belong to one of the world's largest surviving matrilineal cultures. Their living root bridges, grown from rubber fig roots, are on UNESCO's tentative list.

Shillong, the capital, is the base. To the south, Cherrapunji (Sohra) still holds the records for the most rain in a month and a year, with Nohkalikai, India's tallest plunge waterfall, the Mawsmai cave and the trek to Nongriat's double-decker root bridge.

how_to_reach.text: Guwahati airport, the main airport of the Northeast, is the usual gateway; Shillong also has an airport at Umroi.

best_time.text: In Cherrapunji, November to February is the drier season — best for waterfalls, caves and root-bridge treks.

Arunachal Pradesh is the largest of the Northeast's seven sister states, with over 500 orchid species. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, available online as an e-ILP.

items.title: Arunachal
items.body: Arunachal Pradesh is the largest of the Northeast's seven sister states, with over 500 orchid species.

items.title: Inner Line Permit
items.body: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit to enter Arunachal Pradesh; a tourist ILP is valid for 15 days, and can be applied for online as an e-ILP.
Elsewhere in Arunachal Pradesh — Tawang: Tawang sits at about 3,000 m, 448 km by road from Itanagar.
Elsewhere in Arunachal Pradesh — Dirang: Dirang's Thembang is a 9th-century fortified village on UNESCO's candidate list.
Elsewhere in Arunachal Pradesh — Bomdila: Bomdila Monastery (GRL), set up in 1965, has three sections; Bomdila is 160 km from Tezpur and 340 km from Guwahati.
Elsewhere in Arunachal Pradesh — Ziro: Ziro, at about 1,500 m and 165 km from Itanagar, is home to the Apatani and their paddy-cum-fish farming; it was shortlisted for UNESCO in 2012.

body.intro: Several of the Northeast's best places sit near international borders, so check permits before you plan.

sections.text: Indian visitors need an ILP to enter Arunachal. A tourist ILP is valid for 15 days, can be extended, and can be applied for online as an e-ILP.

guides.seoDescription: Plan Tawang: India's largest monastery, Sela Pass at 4,170 m, the war memorials, Bomdila and Dirang on the way, and the Inner Line Permit.

body.intro: Tawang is one of the great Himalayan journeys — plan permits and pace.

sections.heading: The monastery
sections.text: Founded in 1680–81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso at the wish of the 5th Dalai Lama, it is India's largest Buddhist monastery, with a 28-foot Buddha.

sections.heading: The road
sections.text: From Tezpur, the road runs via Bomdila (160 km) and Dirang over the 4,170 m Sela Pass, 78 km before Tawang.

sections.heading: Memorials
sections.text: The Tawang War Memorial honours 2,420 servicemen of 1962; Jaswant Garh, 25 km away, honours rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat.

sections.heading: Permit
sections.text: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, valid 15 days, available online.

guides.seoDescription: Meghalaya's living root bridges: grown from rubber fig roots by the Khasi and Jaintia, on UNESCO's tentative list, and the 3,500-step Nongriat trek.

body.intro: Meghalaya's root bridges are grown, not built.

sections.heading: What they are
sections.text: The Khasi and Jaintia peoples grow these bridges from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees. They are on UNESCO's tentative list.

sections.heading: The Nongriat trek
sections.text: The trek to the double-decker bridge starts in Tyrna and descends about 3,500 steps — and you climb back up.

sections.heading: When to go
sections.text: November to February is the drier season around Cherrapunji.

sections.text: The capital at 1,650 m: MG Marg, Rumtek, and day trips to Tsomgo Lake (12,313 ft) and Nathu La.

sections.heading: North Sikkim
sections.text: Lachung and the Yumthang Valley, flowers late February to mid June, closed December to March; Gurudongmar Lake at 5,430 m.

sections.heading: Pelling
sections.text: Kanchenjunga views at 2,150 m, Pemayangtse Monastery and Khecheopalri Lake.
